Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

SIMP 0.2.0

  • New integrator "minerror2": a two-stage order-two scheme whose free kick weight is fixed at (3 - sqrt(5)) / 4, the value that cancels the leading energy-error term on a harmonic (Gaussian) target. It takes two gradient evaluations per step, conserves energy far better than leapfrog near a Gaussian, and admits larger steps without the stability cliff of the high-order composition schemes.
  • simp_integrate_nonsep() integrates non-separable Hamiltonians (for example Riemannian dynamics with a position-dependent mass) with the generalized (implicit) leapfrog, exposed in C++ as simp::step_implicit in <simp/implicit.h>. For a separable Hamiltonian it reduces to leapfrog.
  • Recovery tests cover the new members: the minerror2 energy cancellation and its order on a nonlinear problem, and the generalized leapfrog’s separable-reduction, energy conservation, and reversibility.

SIMP 0.1.0

First release of SIMP as a symplectic-integration library.

  • simp_integrate() advances a separable Hamiltonian system with a chosen symplectic splitting scheme, returning the endpoint or the full trajectory and, optionally, the total energy along it.
  • simp_schemes() lists the built-in integrators: leapfrog and the Yoshida order 4, 6, and 8 members, generated from leapfrog by triple-jump composition.
  • simp_hmc() runs Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with any of the schemes.
  • Header-only, scalar-templated C++ core in inst/include/simp/ for LinkingTo: SIMP consumers.
